data.body: S1 4b/4c/4d/4e: Authored 7-test contract oracle in tests/unit/test_llm_provider_factory.py. RED evidence: 2x ModuleNotFoundError 'rebar.llm.providers' (genuine absence of the new module) + 1x wrong-type (LLMUnavailableError where contract needs LLMConfigError). NOTE ON RED HONESTY: S1 is a PURE RELOCATION, so 4 of 7 tests pass before AND after by design — they are labelled in-file as SS-A characterization (the regression net that gives 'no behavior change' teeth); only the SS-B new-contract tests could be RED, and were. Held out from implementer: exception-path close, unknown-provider typed error via run(), unknown-provider typed error via session, model_override negative control. Implementer = SEPARATE subagent at STANDARD tier (sonnet) per model tiering; brief carried module-size cap 800 / providers.py<300 / leaf-import rule / deferred heavy imports / ruff E,F,W,I,UP,B since the behavioral oracle cannot see those. Attempt count reported: 1. HELD-OUT VALIDATION: 6/7 pass, 1 FAIL — a genuine over-fit catch. Implementer gated infer_model on session.supports(name), so an unregistered provider never reaches the seam and surfaces as LLMUnavailableError('the LLM provider call failed') instead of LLMConfigError. That misreports an operator config error as an outage. Per 4e-bis this is a FIRST held-out edge failure => NO tier escalation; re-dispatched same tier with a description of the missing contract (3-step factory: registry -> delegate to pydantic-ai infer_provider for openai/google -> LLMConfigError), NOT the test text. Baseline suite before changes: GREEN (exit 0).
